headline: Benchmark design choices shift performance estimates in biomolecular machine learning
label: Benchmark Design Robustness Audits
summary: Four preprints test whether reported computational gains survive alternative splits, negative sets, distance strata and simulated campaigns.
synthesis: The dominant thread is whether reported performance survives changes in evaluation design. The antimicrobial peptide study audits cluster-disjoint versus random splitting and negative-set choice for frozen ESM-2 classifiers, and the β-lactamase study stratifies variant-effect benchmarks by distance for ESM2, ThermoMPNN and structural descriptors on TEM-1 and VIM-2 deep mutational scans. The MLDEx study tests machine-learning-guided directed evolution design choices across 557,143 simulated campaigns on 16 protein fitness landscapes. The gene-network preprint is a different kind of contribution: it presents a certified fixed-confidence best-arm identification method for drug-combination search, together with a benchmark and an AML application. What is new is the emphasis on bounded, design-dependent conclusions rather than single headline scores.
